podcast.body: Released in 1991, this album was a commercial success and had significant repercussions, but it was also highly questionable. It escalated its lyrical content beyond their first album, moving past police brutality and drug dealing to include highly problematic discourses such as sexual violence, mistreatment of women, homophobic attitudes, and even racist sentiments among the band members themselves. The band actively contributed to the banalization of the words "nigga" and "bitch" on this album. Following its release, the band eventually dissolved due to numerous internal conflicts and significant questioning from within Afro-American culture regarding the controversial nature of its content. "tendríamos un segundo albún de la banda en 1991, un segundo albún que sería nigas por life, que por desgracia a pesar de que también fue un buen buen éxito, a pesar de que tuvo mucha repercusión, fue un disco más que cuestionado y sin realmente más que cuestionable."
